sentences.text: Neha Sao D/o Basant Sao Aged About 27 Years
R/o Village Jagdishpur, P.S. Basna, District : Mahasamund,
Chhattisgarh.

------Appellant  VERSUS   State Of Chhattisgarh through - The Station House Officer,
 Police Station - D.D. Nagar, District - Raipur (C.G.).
-------Non-appellants

For appellants : Mr. C.R. Sahu, Advocate  For Non-appellants-State : Mr. Jitendra Shrivastava, G.A.
 SB: Hon'ble Shri Parth Prateem Sahu, Judge  ORDER ON BOARD

This Criminal Appeal is filed by the Appellant under Section 14 (A) (2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 for grant of anticipatory bail as she is apprehending her arrest in connection with Crime No. 310/2023, registered at Police Station - D.D.
Nagar, District - Raipur, Chhattisgarh for offence punishable under Section 376, 376 (2) (n), 511,
294, 323, 506-B, 313, 342, 417, 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and under Section 3 (2) (V) (Va)
of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (as per challan)
(hereinafter referred to as Atrocities Act, 1989).
2. Case of the prosecution is that, vicitm lodged a written report at the concerned police station alleging that the co-accused Parmeshwar Sahu on the pretext of marriage has committed sexual intercourse with her since last 02 years.

When co-accused Parmeshwar Sahu gave mobile number of the victim/complainant to the present appellant, she on mobile phone has threatened that if the complainant/victim would pressurize Parmeshwar Sahu for marriage, she will kidnap her.
Further allegation is that due to the physical relation between co-accused Parmeshwar Sahu and the complainant/victim, she is carrying pregnancy of about 09 months.
Based on the report, F.I.R. was registered against Parmeshwar Sahu, Dileshwar Sahu and the present appellant.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case because she was going to be married with co-accused Parmeshwar Sahu with whom,

sentences.text: Appellant has not committed any offence as alleged.
Co-accused Parmeshwar Sahu has been granted anticipatory bail in Criminal Appeal No. 1811/2023 vide order dated 06.11.2023.
Hence, the appellant may be granted anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, learned State counsel opposes the submission made by learned counsel for the appellant.
However, upon asking, he submits that the allegation against the appellant is only that the appellant gave mobile call and threatened the complainant/victim.

Learned counsel for the State, on asking, further submits that, though, charge-sheet has been filed only against co-accused Dileshwar Sahu, however, there is no seizure of any WhatsApp Chat or WhatsApp phone call.
He further submits that there is no seizure of WhatsApp Chat or details of the WhatsApp call in the mobile phone of the victim.
5. He further contended that in the supplementary statement of the victim, it is stated that the present applicant have abused the victim by her caste.

Upon putting specific query as to whether any allegation of abusing by caste by the appellant is mentioned in the F.I.R. or the statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.? He submits that no such allegation is leveled against the appellant.

6. Pursuant to the notice issued by this Court, notice sent to the complainant/victim is reported to be served upon the brother of the complainant/victim, however, there is no representation on their behalf.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the respective parties.

8. Taking into consideration, the material available in the charge-sheet as submitted by the counsel for the appellant it appears that the report is lodged because co-accused Parmeshwar Sahu who is having physical relation with the victim, refused to marry her and he was engaged with the present applicant and also, was going to marry her.
In the F.I.R., there is no allegation against the appellant of abusing the victim by her caste by the present appellant, it is leveled in supplementary statement.

Co-accused Parmeshwar Sahu with whom, victim was having love relation as also, physical relations has been enlarged on anticipatory bail vide order dated 06.11.2023 in Criminal Appeal No.
1811/2023.
9.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Prathvi Raj Chauhan Vs. Union of India & Ors. reported in (2020) 4 SCC 727, has observed thus:-
"11.

entities.text: Prathvi Raj Chauhan Vs. Union of India & Ors. reported in (2020) 4 SCC 727
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Concerning the applicability of provisions of section 438 Cr.PC, it shall not apply to the cases under Act of 1989.
However, if the complaint does not make out a prima facie case for applicability of the provisions of the Act of 1989, the bar created by section 18 and 18A (i) shall not apply.
We have clarified this aspect while deciding the review petitions.

sentences.text: I would only add a caveat with the observation and emphasize that while considering any application seeking pre-arrest bail, the High Court has to balance the two interests: i.e. that the power is not so used as to convert the jurisdiction into that under Section 438 of the Criminal Procedure Code, but that it is used sparingly and such orders made in very exceptional cases where no prima facie offence is made out as shown in the FIR, and further also that if such orders are not made in those classes of cases, the result would inevitably be a miscarriage of justice or abuse of process of law.

I consider such stringent terms, otherwise contrary to the philosophy of bail,
absolutely essential, because a liberal use of the power to grant pre-arrest bail would defeat the intention of Parliament."
10. Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in case of Rahul Sharma Vs. State of Chhattisgarh reported in 2021 SCC Online Chh. 456 considering decision in case of Prathvi Raj Chauhan (supra)

entities.text: Rahul Sharma Vs. State of Chhattisgarh reported in 2021 SCC Online Chh. 456
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: has observed thus:-
"11. Therefore, in appropriate cases, benefit of anticipatory bail should be admitted to appellant and there is no absolute bar.

12. Considering the overall circumstances of the present case, particularly long standing affair of the appellant and the prosecutrix and that both are major and there was more than one occasion of separation and reunion and finally, lodging of the FIR only when marriage could not materialise because of non-acceptance of relationship of the appellant and the prosecutrix by the family of the appellant and appellant took back seat, in the considered opinion of this Court, present is a case of exceptional nature for admitting the appellant to the benefit of anticipatory bail despite bar created under Section 18 of the Act of 1989."
11.

From the aforementioned decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court as also this High Court, it is appearing that in appropriate cases benefit of anticipatory bail can be extended to appellant in cases of exceptional nature.

12. Taking in consideration, facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegations, submission of the counsel for the appellant as also, submission of the counsel for the State, contents of the F.I.R.,
in the considered opinion of this Court, present is a case of exceptional nature for admitting the appellant to benefit of anticipatory bail.
13. For the foregoing discussions, appeal is allowed.
Order passed by learned Court below is set-aside.

It is directed that in the event of arrest of appellant in connection with crime in question,
she shall be released on anticipatory bail by the Officer arresting her, on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer.

Appellant shall also abide by following conditions:
(i) That, the appellant shall make herself available for interrogation before the Investigating Officer as and when required.
